chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the woman who gives birth (releases the placenta); is it permissible for her to marry before she becomes pure? He said: 'Yes, but her husband may not have sexual intercourse with her until she becomes pure.'

key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: has sexual intercourse with her / consummates the marriage

ai.seo_question: Can a postpartum woman marry before her ritual purification is complete?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the validity of the marriage contract (nikah) and the permissibility of consummation for a postpartum woman. It establishes that while she may legally marry before completing her ritual purification (ghusl), her husband is prohibited from entering into sexual relations with her until she is ritually pure, a ruling derived from the general principle that major ritual impurity restricts marital intimacy.
